> I would also rather use a weak pointer and check if the observed object is still there (`command_interface_.lock()` before access to the interface) because loaned interfaces do not own but observe the object. By using shared_ptr we increase the reference count and extend live time of the object and i am not sure of the consequences here...
> 
> For me it seems like we have more of a lifetime and ownership problem here  because a loanedinterfaces should not outlive the interfaces they are created on.

Yes, I agree with you. Weak_ptr is perfect for this application, but at the same time. I'm worried about the performance costs it might bring. As weak_ptr is lock free but not wait free, so continuous writing to interfaces  might cause issues. 

I'll see if I can test this on TALOS and see if it causes any jitter or not. This can wait until then

_Originally posted by @saikishor in https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/2634#issuecomment-3527339489_
new_candidates.title: Investigate weak_ptr in loaned interfaces

ros2 doctor --report (excerpt; network configuration and the full package list omitted) ```text PACKAGE VERSIONS ament_cmake_pytest : latest=2.5.6, local=2.5.6 launch_testing_ros : latest=0.26.13, local=0.26.13 launch_testing_ament_cmake : latest=3.4.12, local=3.4.12 launch_testing : latest=3.4.12, local=3.4.12 launch : latest=3.4.12, local=3.4.12 PLATFORM INFORMATION system : Linux platform info : Linux-7.0.0-38-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 release : 7.0.0-38-generic processor : x86_64 RMW MIDDLEWARE middleware name : rmw_zenoh_cpp ROS 2 INFORMATION distribution name : jazzy distribution type : ros2 distribution status : active release platforms : {'debian': ['bookworm'], 'rhel': ['9'], 'ubuntu': ['noble']} ``` Python and pytest used for the reproduction (apt `python3-pytest`, not listed by `ros2 doctor`): ```text pytest 7.4.4 Python 3.12.3 ```
### Steps to reproduce issue mkdir repro && cd repro mkdir -p tests .hidden echo 'def test_ok(): pass' > tests/test_ok.py echo 'def test_ignored(): assert False' > tests/test_ignored.py echo 'def test_hidden(): assert False' > .hidden/test_hidden.py source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash python3 -m pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_ignored.py ### Expected behavior `1 passed`: `tests/test_ignored.py` is skipped because of `--ignore`, and `.hidden/` is skipped because pytest's default `norecursedirs` includes `.*`. This is what `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python3 -m pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_ignored.py` prints. #### Actual behavior ```text FAILED .hidden/test_hidden.py::test_hidden - assert False FAILED tests/test_ignored.py::test_ignored - assert False 2 failed, 1 passed ``` Same result with apt's pytest 7.4.4 and with pytest 9.1.1. A `collect_ignore = ["tests/test_ignored.py"]` in `conftest.py` is ignored too. ### Actual behavior FAILED .hidden/test_hidden.py::test_hidden - assert False FAILED tests/test_ignored.py::test_ignored - assert False 2 failed, 1 passed ### Additional information `launch_testing/pytest/hooks.py` now defines: ```python @pytest.hookimpl(tryfirst=True) def pytest_ignore_collect(collection_path=None, path=None, config=None): ... return False ``` `pytest_ignore_collect` is a `firstresult` hook. Because this implementation runs first (`tryfirst`) and returns `False` rather than `None` for ordinary paths, the hook call stops there, and pytest's own implementation in `_pytest/main.py`, which reads `--ignore`, `--ignore-glob`, `collect_ignore` and (on pytest 8+) `norecursedirs`, never runs. On pytest 7.4.4 `norecursedirs` is bypassed as well. The hook comes from #974 (rolling) and its Jazzy backport #1006. Our CI started collecting excluded files right after the Jazzy sync that moved `launch_testing` from 3.4.11 to 3.4.12. I have not run this exact repro against 3.4.11. Related: #979 (the `path` vs `collection_path` hookspec error on pytest >= 8.1) is a different symptom in the same file. This issue is a side effect of the hook rewrite for that class of problem: #974 (rolling) added this `pytest_ignore_collect` to `launch_testing/pytest/hooks.py`, and the Jazzy backport #1006 (merged 2026-09-18) carries it unchanged. The open Humble backport #991 adds the same hook with the same `return False`, so merging it as is would bring this regression to Humble. Impact in practice: a package that keeps a `launch_test` file out of plain pytest with `addopts = --ignore=test/test_x_launch.py` now has it collected and failing at import, and a CI layout that clones dependencies into a dot directory inside the package now runs those dependencies' tests. Suggested fix: return `None` instead of `False` for paths the plugin does not want to ignore (including the `p is None` branch), so the remaining implementations still run. Only `True` should end the call. Workaround until then: a `conftest.py` with its own `@pytest.hookimpl(tryfirst=True) pytest_ignore_collect` that returns `True` for the paths to skip and `None` otherwise. A conftest plugin is registered later, so among `tryfirst` implementations it is called first.
